facts.text: OopsieVerse is a damage-aware, simulator-agnostic framework and benchmark for learning and evaluating safer robot manipulation
OopsieVerse builds on BEHAVIOR-1K/OmniGibson, RoboCasa and RoboSuite
OopsieBench spans OmniGibson (NVIDIA Omniverse) and Robosuite (MuJoCo)
The environment registry's default robot is PandaOmron and its default control frequency is 20
close_drawer is registered with environment class CloseDrawer and damageable class DamageableCloseDrawer
DamageableCloseDrawer constructs the environment with task_name close_drawer
CloseDrawer sets randomize_scene to True, so the scene is randomized per episode
The drawer starts with a door state between 0.95 and 1.0
The close_drawer episode starts with the drawer open
CloseDrawer computes the reward as 10.0 times one minus the mean door state
The success check rejects the episode while any drawer joint position is above 0.05
The success check uses a gripper-to-drawer-root-body distance threshold of 0.75 m
The damageable environment reset returns (observation, info) and reinitializes damage tracking
The damageable environment step returns (observation, reward, done, info)
The observation appends a float32 health array
The proprio vector concatenates 7 joint sines, 7 joint cosines, 3 end-effector positions, 4 quaternion values and 2 gripper positions when those keys are present
The tests build the environment from the registry robot and a composite controller, with camera observations off and the registry control frequency
The teleoperation loop builds the environment action with robot.create_action_vector and steps the environment with the concatenated result
Installation clones RoboSuite and RoboCasa and pip-installs both
The package's declared dependencies are open3d, matplotlib, scipy, tyro, tqdm and numba

determinism.notes: the fake re-seeds Python's random generator on reset(seed) and on cap.world.seed.v1; the upstream damageable reset() takes no seed argument (damagesim/robosuite/damageable_env.py:382) and the clone defines no seed setter, so a real sim deployment would ignore the seed and was not run

gaps: the upstream model is RoboCasa on Robosuite/MuJoCo (docs/oopsiebench.md:3) with rigid-body dynamics and contacts; the fake is an analytic stand-in that models no contacts, friction, actuators, sensors or noise

the fake's seven-value action vector is placeholder test data; the real PandaOmron composite-controller action is assembled at run time (scripts/teleop_robocasa.py:838-845) and its size and bounds are not stated in the clone, so the fake serves an unbounded action space

the fake returns a reduced observation (robot0_eef_pos 3, robot0_gripper_qpos 2, robot0_proprio 23 and one health value); the upstream observation also carries the Robosuite observation keys and a health vector whose length is the number of tracked links (damagesim/core/damageable_env.py:259-269), which is not stated in the clone

no cameras, depth, segmentation or rendering: the upstream test and teleoperation entry points used here set use_camera_obs=False (scripts/tests/test_robocasa.py:54-57, scripts/teleop_robocasa.py:1006-1007)
no snapshot or restore: the clone defines no get_state/set_state on the environment
the fake seeds its own generator; the upstream reset() takes no seed (damagesim/robosuite/damageable_env.py:382), so the sim backend would ignore cap.world.seed.v1 and the reset seed

the sim backend was not run: close_drawer is registered in the clone's own EnvironmentRegistry (oopsiebench/envs/registry.py:65) and not with gymnasium.register, so gymnasium.make('close_drawer') is not provided; a real deployment needs an EnvironmentRegistry factory
the fake's end-effector gain, door travel, start pose and health damage rate are placeholders, and the gripper-distance half of _check_success (close_drawer.py:138-142) is not modelled
no physical device is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware; the fake was not compared with a RoboCasa run

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: the runtime refuses step and reset after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the last world state stays readable
